title: PM Anwar announces cabinet reshuffle amid coalition speculation
content: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today announced a minor cabinet reshuffle, moving two deputy ministers to different portfolios. The move comes amid growing speculation about coalition stability following recent by-election results. Political analysts suggest the reshuffle is aimed at strengthening the unity government's position ahead of state elections.

title: MACC investigates senior ministry official over procurement irregularities
content: The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission has launched an investigation into a senior official at the Ministry of Works over alleged procurement irregularities involving road projects worth RM50 million. MACC Chief Commissioner confirmed the investigation and said several documents have been seized. The official has not been arrested but is cooperating with investigations.

title: China's ambassador meets Foreign Minister over South China Sea incident
content: China's ambassador to Malaysia held a closed-door meeting with Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan this morning following reports of a coast guard encounter near Luconia Shoals. Both ministries issued brief statements saying the discussion was 'cordial and constructive.' Diplomatic sources suggest Malaysia has lodged a protest note over the incident.

title: Budget 2027: Finance Ministry signals subsidy rationalization ahead
content: The Finance Ministry has signaled further subsidy rationalization in Budget 2027, with fuel and electricity subsidies expected to be targeted. Second Finance Minister Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah said the government is committed to fiscal consolidation while protecting vulnerable groups. Economists estimate the move could save RM15 billion annually but may impact inflation.

title: NGO plans protest over religious conversion controversy
content: A coalition of NGOs has announced plans to hold a protest next week over the recent controversy surrounding alleged forced religious conversions. The rally, expected to draw thousands, will demand clearer federal-state guidelines on conversion matters. Police have yet to comment on the permit application.

title: PETRONAS reports record quarterly profits on higher oil prices
content: National oil company PETRONAS reported record quarterly profits of RM25 billion, driven by higher oil prices and increased production. The GLC announced it will contribute RM10 billion to the federal budget, exceeding earlier estimates. CEO Tengku Muhammad Taufik said the company is also investing heavily in renewable energy transition.

title: Parliament passes amendments to Employment Act 1955
content: Parliament today passed amendments to the Employment Act 1955, introducing stronger protections for gig workers and increasing penalties for employers who violate labor laws. The bill was supported by both government and opposition MPs. Human Resources Minister said the changes will benefit over 2 million workers nationwide.

title: Floods in east coast states displace 5,000 residents
content: Continuous monsoon rains have caused flooding in several districts in Kelantan and Terengganu, displacing over 5,000 residents to relief centers. The Meteorological Department has issued orange alert warnings for the next 48 hours. Prime Minister has directed relevant agencies to ensure adequate relief supplies and monitoring.
